subject.title: feat(memorySearch): Support multimodal embedding with gemini-embedding-2-preview

question: Should OpenClaw expand multimodal memory beyond opt-in image/audio files in `memorySearch.extraPaths` into PDF/video files and remembered session attachments, and what consent, retention, deletion, provider-upload, and reindexing contract should gate it?
rationale: The remaining behavior is technically feasible, but it changes how user media is uploaded to remote embedding providers and retained in searchable memory, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Design gated media memory first
options.body: Define supported modalities, explicit opt-in consent, retention/deletion behavior, provider limits, result presentation, and reindex/migration behavior before implementation.

options.title: Limit core to shipped subset
options.body: Keep core behavior at image/audio files under `extraPaths` and defer broader attachment/PDF/video memory until a stronger maintainer-sponsored direction appears.

options.title: Expand only extraPaths modalities
options.body: Allow a narrower follow-up for PDF/video files under `extraPaths` while explicitly excluding remembered chat-attachment retention for now.

recommendation.title: Design gated media memory first
recommendation.body: Define supported modalities, explicit opt-in consent, retention/deletion behavior, provider limits, result presentation, and reindex/migration behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision lands closest to the shipped multimodal memory boundary introduced through the image/audio `extraPaths` work.
